In The High Court Of Orissa, Cuttack
 L.A.A. No.34 of 2016
 Union of India ....... Appellant

 For Appellant : K.C. Jena, Cgc

 Addl. Standing Counsel

 Coram: Justice Sanjay Kumar Mishra

Though the matter is listed under the heading "For  Hearing" and tracking report available on record indicates  that notices were duly served on the Private Respondent  Nos.3 to 7 on 09.02.2024, 09.02.2024, 12.02.2024,
 12.02.2024 and 09.02.2024 respectively, the said  Respondents go unrepresented when the matter is called for  hearing.

Since this is an Appeal of the year 2016 and the  photocopy of the LCR has already been received, on consent  of the learned Central Government Counsel for the Union of  India/Appellant so also learned Counsel for the State/Respondent, matter is taken up for hearing and final disposal.
2. This appeal has been preferred by the Appellant/Union Union Of India vs Land Acquisition Officer on 12 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/83120389/
1 of India challenging the judgment dated 27.01.2016 passed in L.A. Misc. Case No.65 of 2008 vide which, the referral Court enhanced the compensation amount to Rs.2150/- per decimal from Rs.1346/- per decimal awarded by the Land Acquisition Officer.

3. The brief background facts, which led to filing of this Appeal, are that the land in question was acquired by the State Government for Khurda Road-Bolangir New B.G. Rail Link Project vide notification dated 26.09.2006 under Section 4(1) of L.A. Act, 1894.

The land of the present Respondents,
measuring an area of Ac.0.23 decimals Kisam-Sarad Dofassli(iii) under Mouza-Dhenkana, P.S/District-Nayagarh,
was acquired for the said purpose.
A sum of Rs.44,968/- has been awarded in favour of the Respondents (Petitioners before the Court below) as compensation and other benefits.

4. The present Appeal has been preferred challenging the said judgment dated 27.01.2016 in L.A. Misc. Case No.65 of L.A.A. No.34 of 2016 Page 2 of 5  2008 basically on the ground that the Court below decided the question of enhancement of compensation by misconstruing the Exhibits relied upon by the Appellant and the benchmark valuation was not taken into account while passing the judgment.

5. On perusal of the impugned judgment, it is ascertain that the Court below, relying on Ext.A and the judgment of the Apex Court in Nirmal Singh Vs. State of Haryana,
reported in AIR 2015 SC 453 so also Mehrawal Khewaji Trust (Regd.), Faridkot & others Vrs. State of Punjab,
reported in 2012 (II) CLR (S.C.)-41, held that the additional value shall be calculated @ Rs.150/- per decimal of land.

sentences.text:
So in total the value of the land in question was determined @
Rs.2150/- per decimal.

Para-12 and 12.2 of the impugned judgment, being relevant,
are extracted below:-
 "12.

To reach at a conclusion about the  market value this court has to imagine the L.A.A. No.34 of 2016 Page 3 of 5  amount what a bone fide purchaser will offer to  purchase the land in question to the seller.
Working sheet (Ext. A) gives consideration  amount for each of transactions those took  place in sample period.
The working sheet  shows that value of Sarada-III Dofasali land
in the last half of the year 2005 and first  half of 2006 was Rs. 2,00,000/- per acre.

This was the highest value paid for any  land in sample year of 2003 to 2006 (up to  the date of notification U/s. 4(i) of L.A.Act,
 dtd.26.09.2006).
This is the  contemporaneous to the period to date of  notification U/s. 4 (i) of LA Act.

Such  baseline value added with some price  considering the little advantageous location  of the agricultural land in question would  be the proper approach to fix the market  value for the land in question.

12.2. The working sheet reveals that during  the sample period of 2003-06 in Dhenkana  village, the highest rate of transaction was of Rs.

3  2,00,000/- per acre (one acre-100 decimals).

sentences.text: The  claimants assert that there are some public  road near the land in question.
That may  also fetch some additional value to the land  in question.
That additional value shall be  calculated at Rs.150/- per decimal of land.
So in  total the value of land in question is determined  at the rate of Rs.2150/- (rupees two thousand  one hundred and fifty) per decimal.
In my L.A.A. No.34 of 2016 Page 4 of 5  consideration that amount would be the proper  market value for the land in question."
(Emphasis Supplied)
6. In view of the specific finding of the Court below so also settled position of law and the evidence on record, this Court is not inclined to interfere with the impugned judgment.
7. Accordingly, the Appeal stands dismissed.
8. Registry is directed to communicate a copy of this order to the Court below so also to the private Respondents.
